verdict.rationale: Exa's public pricing docs list per-request rates: Deep Search at $12–15 per 1k requests, Answer at $5 per 1k requests, and contents at $1 per 1,000 pages beyond 10 results. They describe the model as pay-as-you-go, charged per request, with no subscription or minimum spend, and a self-serve free tier that needs no payment method, so no sales contact is required. Missing for 10: an explicit per-1k price for standard/Lite search and quantified Agent pricing in the pack, plus independent corroboration of the pricing transparency.

support.subject: As a developer, I can see clear per-request or per-credit pricing without talking to sales

citations.quote: Exa is pay-as-you-go. There is no subscription and no minimum spend: you load credits and are charged per request
Deep Search $12–15 / 1k requests Multi-step research with structured outputs and citations.
Answer $5 / 1k requests An LLM answer to a question, with citations.
at no extra charge up to 10 results per search ($1/1000 pages afterwards)
The Free Tier gives you $10 in credits (up to 2,500 Lite searches) the day you sign up
